Our current [BNN](../bnn-emnist-ice40/index.qmd) classifies a 28 × 28 bitmap into one of 47 EMNIST balanced classes. That gives us a 6-bit 'class' register and nothing to look at. This post covers the output hardware I'm adding around his design: a VGA screen showing the predicted character and a top-10 bar graph, plus a bank of 16 × 14-segment displays that acts as a rolling character log. Both are driven by a second iCE40 UP5K, chained to the BNN's UP5K over SPI.

| | |
|---|---|
| Chips | 2 × iCE40 UP5K (FPGA_A + FPGA_B) |
| FPGA_A pins used | 18 of ~39 (5 SPI from MCU + 10 VGA + 3 link) |
| FPGA_B pins used | 34 of ~39 (3 link + 31 display multiplex) |
| VGA resolution | 640 × 480 @ 60 Hz |
| 14-seg displays | 16 (4 modules × 4 digits), common anode |
| Latency per character | ~820 µs end-to-end |
| External parts | VGA connector + 8 R DAC · 14-seg driver board |

## The ask

Three things need to happen when the BNN finishes an inference:

1. **The predicted character** has to appear on the vga display .
2. **Debug visibility** — on a 47-class problem, knowing the top-1 answer is often not enough. If "a" and "o" are neck and neck, wewant to see both scores.
3. **Short-term memory** — a rolling log of the last several characters recognized, so a demo reads as writing a word, not firing one-off classifications.

The VGA display covers (1) and (2). The 14-seg bank covers (3).

## Why one UP5K can't do it alone

The BNN already uses most of the SPRAM, 7 of 30 EBR blocks, and roughly 5 GPIO for the MCU SPI link. The UP5K on the UPduino has about 39 usable GPIO total. Adding VGA and a 16-digit display bank to the same chip violates the pin budget:

| Scheme | Display pins | SPI | VGA | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Direct static drive on 16 × 14-seg | 240 | 5 | 10 | **255** |
| 16-way multiplex on FPGA (shared 15-seg bus + 16 digit selects) | 31 | 5 | 10 | **46** |
| External shift-register chain (74HC595) | 3 | 5 | 10 | **18** |
| Dedicated driver IC (HT16K33) | 2 | 5 | 10 | **17** |

Only the bottom two rows fit on one UP5K, and each has a cost I want to avoid — details in [Alternatives I considered](#alternatives-i-considered) below.

The cleaner move is to split the output hardware onto a second UP5K. FPGA_A still runs the BNN and drives the VGA; FPGA_B owns the 14-seg bank. The pin budget then becomes:

| | FPGA_A | FPGA_B |
|---|---|---|
| SPI from MCU | 5 | — |
| VGA | 10 | — |
| SPI link to the other FPGA | 3 | 3 |
| 14-seg multiplex | — | 31 |
| **Total** | **18** | **34** |

Both fit with room to spare.

Rust arrows carry data; purple arrows carry new signals introduced by the output hardware (not present in Pierce's original design).

### Section 1: VGA on FPGA_A

VGA has to be driven by the FPGA. A 640 × 480 @ 60 Hz signal is a 25.175 MHz pixel stream with sync pulses on exact cycle boundaries.

There is no framebuffer. 640 × 480 × 1 bpp = 38 KB, and the BNN has already taken most of SPRAM and EBR. Instead, pixels are generated on-the-fly from scanline logic:

- **Big character readout.** An 8 × 16 bitmap font sits in one EBR block (128 characters × 16 bytes = 2 KB). For each pixel inside the character region, look up `font[predicted_class][v_within_char]` and pick bit `h_within_char`. Scaling to a ~64 × 128 pixel glyph is a shift on the within-char coordinates.
- **Bar graph.** Keep the top 10 scores in a 10-entry register (10 × 10 bits). For each pixel, compute `bar_index = (hcount - bar_x0) / bar_width`. If the pixel is inside a bar's x range and below the bar's top, light it.
- **Class labels under the bars.** Reuse the character ROM, one glyph per bar.

The only new BNN-side logic is a **top-10 sorted-insert buffer** sitting beside Pierce's existing argmax. On each of the 47 output-layer scores, the buffer either drops the new score into its sorted position or discards it; linear-search insert, 10 compares, ≤ 10 cycles per score. Total overhead: 470 cycles. 

The VGA controller itself is seven small modules under one wrapper:

| Module | Job | Rough LOC |
|---|---|---|
| `vga_timing` | HSYNC/VSYNC counters, visible-region flag | 40 |
| `font_rom` | 128 × 16-byte ASCII glyph table in EBR | 20 + hex file |
| `class_to_ascii` | 47-entry combinational LUT | 50 |
| `char_renderer` | Big-glyph pixel decision | 60 |
| `bar_renderer` | Bar + label pixel decision | 80 |
| `vga_compositor` | Merge → RGB | 30 |
| `vga_top` | Wrapper + vblank snapshot register | 50 |

### Section 2: 14-seg bank on FPGA_B

Sixteen 14-segment displays, driven in a 16-way multiplex: 15 segment lines shared across all displays as a common bus, 16 digit-select lines enabling one display at a time. At any instant, exactly one display is lit, and the segment bus carries that display's pattern.

Scan math:

- Human flicker fusion is ~60–90 Hz; shooting for200 Hz per digit (can go higher to 500 Hz).
- 200 Hz per digit × 16 digits = 3.2 kHz digit switch rate, so each digit gets a 312 µs slot. At 48 MHz FPGA clock that's 15,000 cycles per slot — thousands of cycles of margin for dead-time insertion and bus updates.
- Dead time of 1–10 µs between digit transitions prevents ghosting from the previous pattern bleeding onto the new digit.

The brightness problem is harder than the flicker problem. At 1/16 duty, average segment current is peak / 16, so to look as bright as a static display each segment needs ~150 mA **peak**. Driving an "8" lights 10 segments at once: 10 × 150 mA = 1.5 A peak flowing through a single digit-select line. Neither the UP5K's 8 mA/pin source current nor its 24 mA sink can survive that, so the FPGA pins only control the display through a transistor layer. The driver board BOM:

| Function | Discretes | Chip-based |
|---|---|---|
| High-side (digit anode) drive | 16 PNP + 16 base R | 2 × UDN2981 |
| Low-side (segment cathode) drive | 15 NPN + 15 base R | 2 × ULN2803 |
| Segment current limit | 15 R | 15 R |
| **Totals** | **31 transistors + 46 R** | **4 ICs + 15 R** |

I'll go with the IC option if the stockroom has them. Two `UDN2981` and two `ULN2803` replace the 31 discretes and 31 of the base resistors; the 15 current-limit resistors still live on the board, sized for the display's forward voltage at ~150 mA peak.

FPGA_B's logic is four small modules: SPI slave (to receive each new character from FPGA_A), a 16-byte ring buffer, a 128-entry ASCII → 16-bit segment-pattern ROM in one EBR block, and a scan FSM.

### Section 3: Inter-FPGA link

Three wires between the two chips: `SCK`, `MOSI`, `CS`. No `MISO` — the character stream only goes A → B, and B has nothing to report back that the overall system needs. FPGA_A runs the master, FPGA_B the slave. SPI clock rate is not time-critical; 5–10 MHz is fine. Payload per inference is 16 bits (`{position[3:0], char[7:0]}` with 4 bits padding, or a full 16-byte frame if we switch to batch updates), which takes ~4 µs at 5 MHz.

Each FPGA uses its own HSOSC as its main clock. The SPI SCK is its own domain.

## Alternatives I considered

| Option | Why I didn't pick it |
|---|---|
| **74HC595 shift-register chain on bare displays** | 32 chips, ~480 wires between them and the displays, and HC595s don't like the peak currents 14-seg displays want. Breadboard-infeasible at this scale. A PCB would work but is out of scope for now. |
| **HT16K33 driver chip (Adafruit quad 14-seg backpacks)** | Would work — 4 backpacks on one I²C bus, 2 pins total — but it moves the whole display-driving story off the FPGA.|
| **Single-UP5K FPGA-side multiplex for everything** | Multiplex alone fits (36 pins) but there's no room left for VGA. If we drop the 14-seg bank the VGA solution survives on one chip, but the whole point of this post was to keep both outputs. |
| **MAX6955 (ASCII-in LED driver)** | Nicest of the dedicated chips (send an ASCII byte, get a lit digit) but availability through the class stockroom is uncertain, and it carries the same "chip does the work" tradeoff as the HT16K33. |

## What's left to write

The BNN is already specified across the [earlier post](../bnn-emnist-ice40/index.qmd) and `bnn_top.drawio`. Everything below is new RTL on top of that:

| Module | Chip | Status | Rough LOC |
|---|---|---|---|
| `top10_buffer` | FPGA_A | new | 70 |
| `vga_top` + submodules | FPGA_A | new | 430 |
| `spi_master` (link) | FPGA_A | new | 30 |
| `spi_slave` (link) | FPGA_B | new | 40 |
| `char_buffer` | FPGA_B | new | 20 |
| `font_rom` (14-seg) | FPGA_B | new | 20 + hex file |
| `scan_fsm` | FPGA_B | new | 50 |

Plus the external driver board (PCB or protoboard), a VGA breakout with the 8-resistor DAC ladder, and testbenches for each FPGA independently.
